record_body:
ACCOUNT SUMMARY
- Lumenworks evaluating Redwood for high-volume summarization + internal support assistant. Primary driver: reduce inference unit cost while keeping reliability and output format stable.
- They specifically asked for route-scoped quantization enablement (batch summarization OK to be more aggressive; interactive chat + JSON-mode routes must be conservative).
- Current posture: enterprise evaluation w/ security review in progress. Likely path: Redwood Dedicated in EU + VPC/Private control plane option depending on InfoSec sign-off.

FIRMOGRAPHICS / ENVIRONMENT
- HQ: EU (Germany); customers across EU/UK.
- Deployment constraints: prefers VPC endpoint / private connectivity; “no public internet egress from app cluster.”
- Data residency: EU processing required; asks for region pinning + audit evidence.
- Compliance: ISO 27001 aligned; requires vendor SOC 2 report and security questionnaire.

PRIMARY USE CASES (from calls)
- Batch summarization: customer tickets, long-form case notes; asynchronous workloads can tolerate higher latency, wants max $/token efficiency.
- Support-agent: interactive; strict latency sensitivity; must preserve instruction following.
- Doc search: embeddings + rerank (secondary, not in initial POC).
- Report generation: structured outputs (JSON) for downstream systems.

KEY REQUIREMENTS / SUCCESS CRITERIA
- Quantization Profile Library:
  - Must be opt-in (no default-on changes).
  - Must support route-level toggles + canary percentage rollout.
  - Must have fast rollback (manual + ideally auto-disable on regression signals).
  - Must be able to exclude specific routes (JSON mode + tool-calling) from int4; int8 may be acceptable.
- Operational safety:
  - Audit log entries for every config change (who/what/when) incl. canary setting changes.
  - Clear precedence: org vs customer vs route overrides (they run multiple internal business units).
  - Ability to “pin” model version + quant profile version for regulated workflows.
- Observability:
  - Needs metrics segmented by route + by quantized vs baseline execution.
  - Wants per-route error budget impact view during canaries (p95 latency + 5xx + output-format drift signals).
- Security:
  - SSO/SAML required for Console; SCIM “nice to have.”
  - KMS integration for any keys; asks how profile artifacts are protected and verified.
  - Artifact integrity: explicitly asked “are profiles signed and verified by the runtime?”
  - Retention controls: trace/log retention configurable; need DPA language.

NOTES (CALL QUOTES / COLOR)
- From technical deep dive: “We want the cost win, but only for the ‘background summarizer’ routes. If JSON breaks, our downstream pipeline breaks.”
- Security lead concern: route toggles must be auditable and reversible; asked for incident playbook and proof that fallback to baseline is automatic when incompatibility detected.
- Platform team asked if they can enforce a policy: disallow int4 for any route tagged ‘customer-facing’.

RECENT ACTIVITY TIMELINE
- 2025-11-14: Intro call (Ava Chen + Markus Klein). Identified cost pressure; they asked about quantization roadmap + safety mechanisms.
- 2025-12-03: Shared initial architecture notes for VPC connectivity + Dedicated capacity options.
- 2026-01-09: Technical deep dive (Fireflies: ff_b18d77_quantization_profiles_technical_deep_dive). Discussion focused on profile scoping by hardware + safe fallback.
- 2026-01-23: Security questionnaire received; started review. InfoSec asked for details on artifact signing + audit logs.
- 2026-02-04: Follow-up on quantization library: requested canary control in Console (slider/percentage) + API support for automation.
- 2026-02-11: Shared internal notes on planned monitoring/auto-disable signals (referenced SRE dashboard requirements doc).
- 2026-02-18: Customer reported JSON-mode regression during their own testing with a separate vendor; reiterated that route-level disable must be immediate and not require redeploy.

OPEN QUESTIONS
- Which EU region(s) are acceptable for their residency requirements (Frankfurt vs Dublin) and whether they require single-region failover.
- Whether they want Redwood Private (VPC control plane) immediately vs after initial Dedicated rollout.
- Final POC scope: which routes are included, and whether we run int8 only for the first phase.

RISKS / WATCHOUTS
- High sensitivity to structured output regressions (JSON mode/tool-calling). Need to propose a conservative rollout plan: start with int8 on batch summarization routes only, with 5–10% canary and explicit rollback criteria.
- They will likely require a documented threat model/controls for profile distribution (signing, verification, RBAC for publishing), plus evidence of audit logs for activation.

NEXT STEPS (INTERNAL)
- Ava: send proposed POC plan + timeline; include explicit canary/rollback flow and audit logging story.
- Markus: prepare security deep dive agenda (profile artifact signing/verification, audit logs, config precedence).
- Pull in: Sean Gallagher (SRE) for rollback/monitoring discussion; Marcus Lin for security review alignment if needed.

NEXT STEPS (CUSTOMER)
- Schedule security deep dive + deliver written answers on (1) profile signing/verification, (2) audit trail for route toggles, (3) auto-fallback behavior on incompatibility, (4) EU data residency controls.
